explanation_en: "Quer dizer" is one of the most common filler and clarifying phrases in Portuguese, equivalent to "I mean" or "that is to say." It is used to correct oneself, elaborate on a point, or draw a logical conclusion. While very common in speech, it should be used sparingly in highly formal writing.

examples.en_text: The project has to be ready tomorrow, which means we have a lot of work today.
examples.target_text: O projeto tem de estar pronto amanhã, quer dizer, temos muito trabalho hoje.

examples.en_text: I really like this jacket, I mean, the blue one, not the black one.
examples.target_text: Eu gosto muito deste casaco, quer dizer, do azul, não do preto.

examples.en_text: Does that mean we don't need to buy the tickets anymore?
examples.target_text: Quer dizer que nós já não precisamos de comprar os bilhetes?

examples.en_text: She said she was going to arrive late, meaning she will only arrive after dinner.
examples.target_text: Ela disse que ia chegar atrasada, quer dizer, só chega depois do jantar.

examples.en_text: The report is almost ready, I mean, I still need to review the last page.
examples.target_text: O relatório está quase pronto, quer dizer, ainda falta rever a última página.

examples.en_text: The supermarket is closed today because it's a holiday, which means we have to go tomorrow.
examples.target_text: O supermercado está fechado hoje por ser feriado, quer dizer que temos de ir amanhã.

explanation_en: "Não faz sentido" is the standard way to say "it doesn't make sense" or "it's pointless." Learners often incorrectly try to translate "it doesn't make sense" literally using "fazer senso," which is incorrect in Portuguese. It is highly versatile and used in all registers.

examples.en_text: It makes no sense to buy a new car if you barely leave the house.
examples.target_text: Não faz sentido comprar um carro novo se você quase não sai de casa.

examples.en_text: To me, it made no sense at all for her to have changed her mind so quickly.
examples.target_text: Para mim, não fez sentido nenhum ela ter mudado de opinião tão rápido.

examples.en_text: It makes no sense for us to keep arguing over such a small problem.
examples.target_text: Não faz sentido continuarmos a discutir por causa de um problema tão pequeno.

examples.en_text: This new company rule simply makes no sense to the employees.
examples.target_text: Essa nova regra da empresa simplesmente não faz sentido para os funcionários.

examples.en_text: At the time, it made no sense to accept that job offer.
examples.target_text: Na época, não fazia sentido aceitar aquela proposta de trabalho.

examples.en_text: Have you read this paragraph? To me, this makes no sense at all.
examples.target_text: Você já leu este parágrafo? Para mim, isto não faz sentido nenhum.

idiom: com o rabo entre as pernas
explanation_en: "Com o rabo entre as pernas" is a colorful idiom meaning to leave defeated, humiliated, or cowed, just like a frightened dog. It is highly expressive and used in informal or semi-formal political debates to describe a humiliating retreat. It should be avoided in extremely formal or academic writing.

examples.en_text: After arguing with the boss and realizing he was wrong, he went back to his desk with his tail between his legs.
examples.target_text: Depois de discutir com o chefe e perceber que estava errado, ele voltou para a sua mesa com o rabo entre as pernas.

examples.en_text: The opponents talked a lot before the game, but left the field with their tails between their legs.
examples.target_text: Os adversários falavam muito antes do jogo, mas saíram do campo com o rabo entre as pernas.

examples.en_text: He lied to his girlfriend, but when she found out the truth, he had to apologize with his tail between his legs.
examples.target_text: Ele mentiu para a namorada, mas quando ela descobriu a verdade, ele teve de pedir desculpas com o rabo entre as pernas.

examples.en_text: They tried to demand a higher price, but had to accept our proposal with their tails between their legs.
examples.target_text: Eles tentaram exigir um preço mais alto, mas tiveram de aceitar a nossa proposta com o rabo entre as pernas.

examples.en_text: The student who claimed to know everything got a terrible grade and went home with his tail between his legs.
examples.target_text: O aluno que dizia saber tudo tirou uma nota péssima e voltou para casa com o rabo entre as pernas.

examples.en_text: There's no point in being arrogant now if you're going to end up coming back with your tail between your legs.
examples.target_text: Não adianta ser arrogante agora se você vai acabar voltando com o rabo entre as pernas.

explanation_en: This common idiomatic construction uses the verb 'estar' with the prepositional phrase 'de volta' to mean 'to return' or 'to be back.' It is highly versatile and used in both spoken and written Portuguese across all registers. Learners should note that 'de volta' remains invariable, while the verb 'estar' conjugates to match the subject.

examples.en_text: After two weeks of vacation, I'm finally back at work.
examples.target_text: Depois de duas semanas de férias, finalmente estou de volta ao trabalho.

examples.en_text: The doctor said she is already back home and is doing much better.
examples.target_text: O médico disse que ela já está de volta a casa e está muito melhor.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, your father will be back before dinner.
examples.target_text: Não te preocupes, o teu pai estará de volta antes do jantar.

examples.en_text: We are back in our hometown to visit family.
examples.target_text: Nós estamos de volta à nossa cidade natal para visitar a família.

examples.en_text: My neighbors were away for a month, but I think they are already back.
examples.target_text: Os meus vizinhos estiveram fora durante um mês, mas acho que já estão de volta.

examples.en_text: It's very good to be back at this wonderful restaurant.
examples.target_text: É muito bom estar de volta a este restaurante maravilhoso.

explanation_en: This expression literally translates to 'outside of the common' and is the standard Portuguese equivalent of 'out of the ordinary' or 'unusual.' It can modify nouns or stand alone to describe situations. It is widely used in everyday conversation as well as journalism to describe extraordinary events.

examples.en_text: The weather today is out of the ordinary for this time of year.
examples.target_text: O tempo hoje está fora do comum para esta época do ano.

examples.en_text: She has an extraordinary talent for painting.
examples.target_text: Ela tem um talento fora do comum para a pintura.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, nothing out of the ordinary happened during your absence.
examples.target_text: Não se preocupe, não aconteceu nada de fora do comum durante a sua ausência.

examples.en_text: The traffic this morning was out of the ordinary, it took me almost an hour to get to work.
examples.target_text: O trânsito hoje de manhã estava fora do comum, demorei quase uma hora a chegar ao trabalho.

examples.en_text: His reaction to the news was a bit out of the ordinary.
examples.target_text: A reação dele à notícia foi um bocado fora do comum.

examples.en_text: That price seems out of the ordinary to me, there must be some mistake.
examples.target_text: Aquele preço parece-me fora do comum, deve haver algum erro.

explanation_en: This emphatic expression is used to conclude an argument or state a fact that the speaker believes is obvious and requires no further explanation. It is the direct equivalent of the English 'simple as that' or 'plain and simple.' It is highly common in spoken Portuguese, op-eds, and informal debates to show assertiveness.

examples.en_text: If you want to learn how to cook, you need to practice every day, simple as that.
examples.target_text: Se você quer aprender a cozinhar, precisa praticar todos os dias, simples assim.

examples.en_text: We don't have money for this project, so we are going to cancel it. Simple as that.
examples.target_text: Nós não temos dinheiro para este projeto, então vamos cancelá-lo. Simples assim.

examples.en_text: If you like her, you should call and tell her the truth, simple as that.
examples.target_text: Se você gosta dela, deveria ligar e dizer a verdade, simples assim.

examples.en_text: To turn on the device, just press this red button. Simple as that.
examples.target_text: Para ligar o aparelho, basta apertar este botão vermelho. Simples assim.

examples.en_text: Want to lose weight? Eat better and exercise more, simple as that.
examples.target_text: Quer perder peso? Coma melhor e faça mais exercícios, simples assim.

examples.en_text: Whoever doesn't arrive on time will miss the train, simple as that.
examples.target_text: Quem não chegar no horário vai perder o trem, simples assim.

explanation_en: 'Perder a graça' means to lose its humor, fun, or appeal. It is commonly used when a joke goes too far, a situation becomes serious, or something simply becomes boring. In this context, the speaker uses it to point out that a funny conspiracy theory becomes distasteful when it starts involving real-life tragedies.

examples.en_text: Playing this video game alone loses its appeal after a while.
examples.target_text: Jogar este videogame sozinho perde a graça depois de algum tempo.

examples.en_text: If you tell the ending of the movie, the story loses all its appeal.
examples.target_text: Se você contar o final do filme, a história perde toda a graça.

examples.en_text: That joke has already lost its fun, nobody laughs at it anymore.
examples.target_text: Aquela piada já perdeu a graça, ninguém mais ri dela.

examples.en_text: The party lost its appeal when my friends decided to leave.
examples.target_text: A festa perdeu a graça quando os meus amigos decidiram ir embora.

examples.en_text: In the beginning it was fun, but after a while the job lost its appeal.
examples.target_text: No início era divertido, mas depois de um tempo o trabalho perdeu a graça.

examples.en_text: Traveling to the same place every year loses its appeal a bit.
examples.target_text: Viajar para o mesmo lugar todos os anos perde um pouco a graça.

explanation_en: This is a very common transitional and hedging phrase in Portuguese, equivalent to 'by all indications,' 'by all accounts,' or 'as far as anyone can tell.' It is widely used in journalism, formal discussions, and everyday speech to state a conclusion based on available evidence without claiming absolute certainty. It is a great B2/C1 filler phrase to sound more native.

examples.en_text: By all accounts, it's going to rain this weekend, so we'd better cancel the picnic.
examples.target_text: Ao que tudo indica, vai chover no fim de semana, por isso é melhor cancelarmos o piquenique.

examples.en_text: By all indications, she is going to be the new director of the marketing department.
examples.target_text: Ao que tudo indica, ela vai ser a nova diretora do departamento de marketing.

examples.en_text: By all accounts, house prices will continue to rise next year.
examples.target_text: Ao que tudo indica, os preços das casas vão continuar a subir no próximo ano.

examples.en_text: The patient is recovering well and, by all indications, will be discharged tomorrow.
examples.target_text: O paciente está a recuperar bem e, ao que tudo indica, terá alta amanhã.

examples.en_text: By all accounts, the new restaurant downtown is already a big success.
examples.target_text: Ao que tudo indica, o novo restaurante no centro da cidade já é um grande sucesso.

examples.en_text: By all indications, our flight is going to be slightly delayed due to bad weather.
examples.target_text: Ao que tudo indica, o nosso voo vai sofrer um ligeiro atraso devido ao mau tempo.

explanation_en: 'Dar a vida' literally means 'to give one's life.' In everyday Portuguese, it is commonly used figuratively to mean dedicating oneself entirely, working tirelessly, or sacrificing everything for a cause, project, or belief. It can be used in professional, personal, or political contexts to show extreme commitment.

examples.en_text: Firefighters are always ready to give their lives for others.
examples.target_text: Os bombeiros estão sempre prontos para dar a vida pelos outros.

examples.en_text: She gave her life for that company, but was never appreciated.
examples.target_text: Ela deu a vida por aquela empresa, mas nunca foi valorizada.

examples.en_text: Any parent would give their life for the safety of their children.
examples.target_text: Qualquer pai ou mãe daria a vida pela segurança dos seus filhos.

examples.en_text: The players gave their all on the field to win the championship.
examples.target_text: Os jogadores deram a vida em campo para ganhar o campeonato.

examples.en_text: He gives his life for music and spends the whole day in the studio.
examples.target_text: Ele dá a vida pela música e passa o dia inteiro no estúdio.

examples.en_text: Many activists are willing to give their lives for the protection of the environment.
examples.target_text: Muitos ativistas estão dispostos a dar a vida pela proteção do meio ambiente.

idiom: tinha alguma coisa a ver com
explanation_en: This is a very common expression used to indicate a connection or relationship between two things. A frequent spelling mistake even among native speakers is writing 'ter haver com' instead of 'ter a ver com'. It can be easily modified with words like 'tudo' (ter tudo a ver com) or 'nada' (não ter nada a ver com).

examples.en_text: I think his decision had something to do with the new project.
examples.target_text: Eu acho que a decisão dele tinha alguma coisa a ver com o novo projeto.

examples.en_text: The cancellation of the event had something to do with the weather forecast.
examples.target_text: O cancelamento do evento tinha alguma coisa a ver com a previsão do tempo.

examples.en_text: Her sadness had something to do with the argument she had yesterday.
examples.target_text: A tristeza dela tinha alguma coisa a ver com a discussão que ela teve ontem.

examples.en_text: The doctor said that the headache had something to do with tiredness.
examples.target_text: O médico disse que a dor de cabeça tinha alguma coisa a ver com o cansaço.

examples.en_text: The problem with my computer had something to do with the latest update.
examples.target_text: O problema no meu computador tinha alguma coisa a ver com a última atualização.

examples.en_text: He didn't want to give details, but the secret had something to do with his family.
examples.target_text: Ele não quis dar detalhes, mas o segredo tinha alguma coisa a ver com a família dele.

explanation_en: 'Dar origem a' is an elegant, B2/C1 level collocation used to describe how one event, institution, or object led to the creation of another. It requires the preposition 'a', which often results in a crasis (crase) when followed by a feminine noun, as in 'deram origem à medicina'. It is highly useful in academic, historical, and journalistic contexts.

examples.en_text: Last week's heavy rains gave rise to several floods in the city.
examples.target_text: As fortes chuvas da semana passada deram origem a várias inundações na cidade.

examples.en_text: These small changes in the project gave rise to a completely new product.
examples.target_text: Estas pequenas alterações no projeto deram origem a um produto completamente novo.

examples.en_text: The student protests gave rise to a new law on education.
examples.target_text: Os protestos dos estudantes deram origem a uma nova lei sobre a educação.

examples.en_text: The disagreements between the partners gave rise to the end of the company.
examples.target_text: Os desentendimentos entre os sócios deram origem ao fim da empresa.

examples.en_text: Many Latin words gave rise to terms we use nowadays.
examples.target_text: Muitas palavras do latim deram origem a termos que usamos hoje em dia.

examples.en_text: Those casual conversations at the cafe gave rise to a great friendship.
examples.target_text: Aquelas conversas casuais no café deram origem a uma grande amizade.

explanation_en: This is a direct translation of 'diamonds in the rough' (literally 'rough diamonds') and is used to describe people, places, or things that have immense potential but are currently unpolished, neglected, or unrecognized. It is a sophisticated metaphorical collocation common in journalism, business, and everyday discussions about potential.

examples.en_text: The coach always manages to find diamonds in the rough in the city's public schools.
examples.target_text: O treinador sempre consegue encontrar diamantes brutos nas escolas públicas da cidade.

examples.en_text: Those interns are diamonds in the rough; they just need a little guidance.
examples.target_text: Aqueles estagiários são diamantes brutos; eles só precisam de um pouco de orientação.

examples.en_text: The music producer travels the country looking for diamonds in the rough for his record label.
examples.target_text: O produtor musical viaja pelo país procurando diamantes brutos para sua gravadora.

examples.en_text: Many students from poor neighborhoods are diamonds in the rough that society ignores.
examples.target_text: Muitos alunos de bairros pobres são diamantes brutos que a sociedade ignora.

examples.en_text: In that small startup, we discovered several programmers who were true diamonds in the rough.
examples.target_text: Naquela pequena startup, descobrimos vários programadores que eram verdadeiros diamantes brutos.

examples.en_text: At the beginning of our careers, we are all diamonds in the rough waiting to be polished.
examples.target_text: No início da carreira, todos nós somos diamantes brutos esperando para ser lapidados.
